habitat: Inshore and intertidal: under stones and in pools on sheltered rocky shores with heavy weed cover; also shallow subtidal rock, 0-15 m (FishBase).

size.maxNote: 13.0 cm TL (FishBase; older editions gave 12 cm). Mature at about 6.5 cm; lives up to about 10 years.

diet: Small bottom-living invertebrates (crustaceans, worms and molluscs).
behaviour: A bottom-living goby that perches on rock and under stones, its pelvic fins joined into a sucking disc; males guard the eggs under stones.
seasonal: Resident year-round on rocky shores; spawns in spring.

identification: Large head with thick lips and high-set eyes; pelvic fins joined into a sucking disc (as in all gobies)
A pale cream, yellow or orange band along the top edge of the first dorsal fin
Mottled dark brown body, darker in breeding males
similar: Black goby (Gobius niger): a black spot at the top front of the first dorsal fin, and longer dorsal rays in males; sand, mud and eelgrass rather than rock
Giant goby (Gobius cobitis): the same rockpool habitat, but grows much larger (to about 27 cm)
anglingMethods: Light rock fishing (LRF): a tiny hook and a scrap of worm or a small soft lure among the rocks and harbour walls
conservation: IUCN global: Least Concern (LC). Of no fisheries interest; catch and release suits it.

habitat: Shallow coastal and estuarine waters, rarely on the shore: among eelgrass (Zostera) or algae on sandy or muddy bottoms (MarLIN); estuaries and lagoons; marine and brackish, 1-96 m, usually 1-50 m (FishBase).

size.maxNote: Up to 17 cm (MarLIN). FishBase gives a maximum of 25.3 cm TL, far above other accounts.

diet: Small bottom-living invertebrates (crustaceans, worms and molluscs).
behaviour: A bottom-living goby of soft ground and eelgrass; tolerates brackish water.

gironde.basis: Range statement (eastern Atlantic from Norway to Mauritania, Mediterranean and Black Sea) and its estuarine habit (MarLIN, FishBase). https://www.marlin.ac.uk/species/detail/1867

identification: Dark brown to nearly black, with darker blotches
A black spot at the top front of the first dorsal fin
In males the rays of the first dorsal fin grow long, beyond the fin's edge
similar: Rock goby (Gobius paganellus): a pale band along the top of the first dorsal fin; rocky shores rather than soft ground
anglingMethods: A tiny hook and a scrap of worm on the bottom in estuaries and harbours
conservation: IUCN global: Least Concern (LC). Of no fisheries interest; catch and release suits it.

habitat: Rocky shores and shallow reefs with seaweed, and seagrass beds; in pools and in the shallow subtidal, usually 1-30 m (MarLIN, FishBase).

size.maxNote: 28 cm SL, common 20 cm (FishBase); MarLIN: to 25 cm, usually under 15 cm.

diet: Small invertebrates picked from rock and weed: crustaceans and molluscs.
behaviour: Males build nests of seaweed among rocks, in crevices or in seagrass, spending weeks on them in spring and early summer and guarding the eggs; some sex reversal (MarLIN, FishBase).
seasonal: Resident year-round; nests and spawns in spring and early summer.

gironde.basis: Range statement (Norway to Morocco; FishBase, MarLIN). Rocky shore near the estuary mouth not verified. https://www.fishbase.se/summary/59

identification: A dark comma-shaped mark just behind the eye
A dark spot on the wrist of the tail (caudal peduncle)
Females and young brown; breeding males green and blue, with bright blue lines on the head
similar: Ballan wrasse (Labrus bergylta): grows much bigger, without the mark behind the eye or the spot on the tail
Goldsinny (Ctenolabrus rupestris): a black spot on the upper side of the tail wrist and at the front of the dorsal fin
anglingMethods: Light rock fishing (LRF): worm, ragworm or a small soft lure among the weedy rocks and harbour walls
conservation: IUCN global: Least Concern (LC). Taken in some places as cleaner fish for salmon farms, where local minimum sizes and seasons apply; best returned.
